notes: Two Nano RP2040 Connect boards: nano1 is the peripheral (with button), nano2 is the central (no extra circuit, only USB). Board is a new part type with only the ports used (D2, GND, USB).
The BLE link between boards is wireless and not represented as an edge.
Image orientation: rows f-j appear at the top half of the breadboard and rows a-e at the bottom, so top half = bank 'b' and bottom half = bank 't'.

Hole positions read from the image: GND wire goes to the top negative rail (tn.1); a second dark wire runs from rail tn.8 to column 10 row g; the teal wire from pin 2 goes to column 8 row c (bottom half).
Pushbutton straddles the centre gap in columns 8 and 10; assumed port 1 = top-half pair, 2 = bottom-half pair, l = column 8, r = column 10.
The USB port is modelled as a header-socket kind since no USB port kind is allowed.
Tutorial uses INPUT_PULLUP, so the button connects pin 2 to GND when pressed.
